transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-23
Time: 14:00 UTC
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Alice Monroe (Redwood AE), Raj Patel (Redwood SE), Monica Li (Redwood Product), Mike Reynolds (Verdant CTO), Sarah Kim (Verdant - Sec), Luis Ortega (Verdant Eng), Anna Berg (Verdant Legal)

Summary:
Quick demo of data minimization controls across Redwood API and Console, walkthrough of request logging toggles, redaction options (PII masking and NLP redaction), and how Private/VPC+KMS flows affect storage. Discussed PoC scope and security artifacts requested.

Topics covered: API request storage toggles, ephemeral vs persisted request storage, PII detection & redaction, KMS integration, RBAC for logs, audit export, performance impact of redaction and batching.

Transcript:
[00:00] Alice (Redwood AE): All right thanks everyone for joining, um we got about 45 minutes on the calendar. Quick intros?
[00:12] Mike (Verdant - CTO): Mike here, I'm the CTO at Verdant, we run the platform and we're looking at embedding LLM features into our operator assist flows.
[00:18] Sarah (Verdant - Sec): Sarah, head of security. I'm here for controls, audit and compliance check.
[00:22] Luis (Verdant Eng): Luis, platform eng, I'll own the PoC setup and network side.
[00:26] Alice: Awesome. Raj, do a quick who-you-are?
[00:30] Raj (Redwood SE): Hey all, Raj Patel, SE on the infra team. I'll demo the console toggles and show how API flags map to storage behavior.
[00:38] [00:38] Monica (Redwood Product): Monica - I'll follow on questions about Optimize recommendations later.

[01:05] Alice: High level, Verdant's ask was to see mechanisms to avoid storing PII in logs, options for ephemeral request handling, and how encryption/KMS and VPC options apply. Is that right Mike?
[01:15] Mike: Yep that's it. We're very sensitive to customer PII. We also need to know latency tradeoffs, if redaction slows down inference, and what is retained for debugging.
[01:24] Sarah: Also audit trails. Legal wants proof of who accessed stored requests and how we can purge or export them for e-discovery.

[02:02] Raj: Cool. I'll start in the Console — show the request storage panel. Note: transcription may say "request store" — it's the same tab.
[02:15] [02:15] Raj (screen share): Here we have three main modes: Store Nothing (ephemeral), Store Metadata Only (tokens, latency, route but not text), Store Full (full request+response). Each has fine-grain toggles for retention period and redaction shim.
[02:35] Sarah: So Store Nothing means nothing persists on Redwood side? Even for debugging?
[02:40] Raj: Correct — in Store Nothing, we do not persist user text or model outputs. We keep minimal metrics for billing and per-token counts for usage, those are aggregated. Debugging is trickier — you can enable temporary capture for a session with a TTL and tight RBAC.
[02:58] Mike: Is temporary capture encrypted differently?
[03:02] Raj: It's stored encrypted at rest with customer-specific KMS if you're on Private or Dedicated. On Hosted we use our managed KMS but for enterprise customers we offer a bring-your-own-key option. There was a bit of slip in the transcript earlier: we said BYOK, that's bring-your-own-key (K M S).
[03:21] [03:21] Luis: On VPC/private, how does network egress look? Do logs ever go out of the VPC?
[03:27] Raj: With Private deployment, the control plane is customer-managed and logs remain inside the VPC unless you opt into forwarding. For hosted accounts, we have options to forward to your SIEM via secure connector.

[04:02] [04:02] Raj (demo): Now redaction. Two approaches: deterministic masking (regex/token redact) and NLP-based PII detection with heuristics. You can stack them. For PII detection we use on-device models that identify names, SSNs, account numbers, etc. There's a confidence threshold you can tune.
[04:25] Sarah: The NLP detector — is that run pre or post inference? Will it impact latency?
[04:30] Raj: Good question. Option A: pre-filter before it's sent to the model — that adds ~15-30ms on our test infra depending on payload size. Option B: post-process redaction after the model returns, which has less impact on model latency but means the full text briefly existed in memory during inference. For high compliance customers we recommend pre-filter plus ephemeral request storage so nothing persists.
[04:55] Mike: Hm, 30ms is fine, but we have some hot paths where p95 needs to be <120ms so that's tight.
[05:02] Raj: Understood. We can run a focused benchmark as part of the PoC with your seq-len distribution. We'll also test the Optimize suggestions — quantization and batching — to see if overall token cost comes down while keeping latency within SLOs.

[06:10] [06:10] Monica: Quick note — Optimize can recommend turning on prefix caching for QPS-heavy assistant workloads which reduces tokens and helps latency; caching is compatible with redaction as long as keys are hashed and PII is stripped before cache key generation.
[06:30] Luis: About audit logs — can we get tamper-evident logs and SSO user identity tied to operations?
[06:36] Raj: Yes, audit logs export includes actor identity mapped from your SAML/SCIM SSO. We support push to your SIEM with signed webhooks and optional HSM-signed attestations for tamper evidence.
[06:50] Sarah: And retention policies — if we set retention to 30 days and then decide to purge earlier, is there a hard delete API?
[06:58] Raj: There is a purge API and console action. Purges are also recorded in the audit trail. For Private deployments we can coordinate a secure purge that runs inside your VPC and confirms deletion.

[08:05] [08:05] Mike: Let's talk about the data flow for our edge-case: operator writes incident report containing customer PII into the prompt. We need to ensure that for our regulators, nothing of that content lives beyond 7 days and access is role-limited.
[08:18] Raj: You'd pick ephemeral storage or Store Full with a 7-day TTL, plus RBAC role that restricts access to logs. In the Console's Roles page you can map Redwood roles to your SAML groups and set policy: e.g., only "Security:ViewLogs" can view request content.
[08:36] Anna (Verdant Legal): For e-discovery we might need export of certain sessions — can exports be redacted on export?
[08:43] Raj: Yes you can request redacted exports where PII is masked; we also support annotated exports that include only metadata and a hash pointer to raw session if you have a signed legal hold. We also provide an export manifest for chain-of-custody.

[10:00] [10:00] Raj (demo continues): Now the API flags — two main headers: X-Redwood-Store: none|metadata|full and X-Redwood-Ephemeral-ttl: seconds. There's also an X-Redwood-No-Cache for bypassing KV/cache. Here's curl example...
[10:30] [10:30] Raj (reads): curl -H "Authorization: Bearer ..." -H "X-Redwood-Store: none" -d '{"input":"..."}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
[10:45] Luis: Ok so we can wire that at service layer to always set none for certain routes?
[10:49] Raj: Exactly. You can also enforce server-side policy in the routing layer so even if a client tries to set store=full the policy will override.

[12:00] [12:00] Mike: About encryption keys — if we do BYOK, what does key rotation look like?
[12:07] Raj: We support periodic rotation. On Private deployments you keep the keys and we accept signed key tokens. There's a re-encrypt window where old data is rewrapped; for large stores you can opt for lazy rewrap to avoid downtime.
[12:24] Sarah: Any SOC2 or ISO artifacts we can look at immediately?
[12:28] Alice: Yep we'll email a trimmed SOC2 report plus the System Use snapshot. I'll attach the security whitepaper and the network diagram for the private deployment. Link preview: https://redwood.example.com/security-whitepaper

[14:00] [14:00] Mike: One concern — we have a compliance requirement that all PII must not leave the EU. Can Redwood restrict storage regionally?
[14:08] Raj: Yes we have regional storage controls. On Hosted we can pin data residency to EU regions and on Private it's fully in your network. There's also a routing policy to ensure inference happens in-region; if capacity is constrained we can fallback to a compatible model variant only within allowed regions.

[15:25] [15:25] Monica: Quick demo of the console redaction config: you can toggle regex patterns, add custom patterns, and set low/med/high confidence thresholds for NLP. There's also a preview tool that runs an example and highlights detected entities.
[15:50] Sarah: Does the preview sample get stored?
[15:54] Raj: The preview uses ephemeral capture and is not persisted unless you save it. That's called out in the UI.

[17:10] [17:10] Luis: For the PoC, we'll need a sample of throughput — we're on k8s with bursts to 1.2k qps across aggregator. We want to test batch behavior.
[17:22] Raj: Great. We'll include a benchmark run with batching parameters tuned to your seq-len. We'll also test redaction pre-filter vs post-process to see latency delta at p95.

[19:05] [19:05] Mike: Pricing — what's the delta between using Hosted with Store Full vs Dedicated with BYOK?
[19:12] Alice: Hosted is per-token and request-storage is an add-on at X cents per stored request per day. Dedicated is a committed capacity model — you get lower per-token pricing and the option to keep keys on-prem; there are also setup and monthly capacity fees. We'll send a tailored cost sheet after the call.

[21:00] [21:00] Anna (Legal): Any third-party subprocessors involved in Hosted mode? We need a list.
[21:07] Alice: Yes we'll include subprocessors list in the security package. We use cloud providers and certain CDN partners, all listed in the contract addendum.

[23:00] [23:00] Sarah: Are there pre-built Data Loss Prevention rules we can import? We have internal regexes for customer ids — can we upload those?
[23:08] Raj: You can upload custom patterns via the Console or API and apply them to a workspace policy. We'll add an example in the PoC template.

[25:40] [25:40] Raj (demo): Now RBAC and audit example: show the audit event where Luis purged a session — it logs actor, timestamp, session-id, action and outcome. The UI shows a signed hash for each audit event.
[26:05] Luis: Nice. That signed hash is useful.

[28:00] [28:00] Mike: Anything about legal holds? If a session is on legal hold can it be prevented from purge?
[28:06] Raj: Yes we have legal hold tags. Tagging a session prevents purge until hold is removed and it's captured in the custody manifest.

[30:12] [30:12] Monica: Quick Optimize note — when redaction is on pre-filter, and you use prefix caching, we ensure cache keys are computed after redaction so PII never ends up in cache. There's a config checkbox for that.

[31:40] [31:40] Anna: For the export manifest chain-of-custody do you include S3 object checksums and Vault key ids?
[31:47] Raj: Yes manifests include object checksum, storage location, key id, and time-of-export.

[33:20] [33:20] Mike: Are there controls for developer sandbox environments? We don't want dev logs to leak prod data.
[33:26] Raj: You can enforce workspace-level policies and have separate sandboxes. We recommend defaulting dev to Store Metadata Only.

[35:00] [35:00] (brief cross talk) Speaker 5: sorry can I ask about retention tapering — like auto downsample old logs?
[35:08] Raj: We offer downsampling: after N days you can convert full logs to metadata-only or hashed blobs, reducing storage costs while preserving audit indices.

[36:40] [36:40] Mike: Ok let's nail PoC scope. We want: 1) Proof that redaction pre-filter meets p95 latency target under our workload, 2) Validate BYOK integration and regional storage to EU, 3) Demonstrate purge and export flows and audit, 4) Cost estimate for 6-week pilot.
[36:56] Raj: We'll produce a PoC plan doc and bench scripts.

[38:10] [38:10] Alice: Recap of next steps: we'll send security pack + subprocessors, PoC plan and pricing, Raj will prepare the config template and benchmark runner, Verdant to share sample payloads and SLOs.
[38:25] Mike: Sounds good. Aim for kickoff week of 12/7.

[40:00] [40:00] Anna: One legal question quick — deletion certification: can Redwood provide a signed deletion certificate after purge?
[40:07] Raj: Yes for enterprise we can provide signed deletion attestations from the HSM and include a manifest of deleted object checksums. We'll include that in the security pack.

[41:50] [41:50] Monica: I'll also attach UI screenshots showing the redaction threshold settings and export manifest so you can share with compliance.

[43:30] [43:30] Luis: I'll send the exact QPS shape and a couple sample prompts, plus our SAML metadata for test account.

[45:00] [45:00] Alice: Great thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the documents and get the kickoff scheduled. Thanks for your time.
[45:10] Mike: Thanks all, bye.
